info.title: Kitchen Sink API
info.description:
The HTTP API of the `kitchen-sink` app, built with TypedPress and served under `/__tp/api/v1` on its WordPress site.

Each request is dispatched to the WordPress REST route behind it, which enforces the app's access rules, field rules, validation and hooks; this API gives the requests and answers one plain shape.

A successful answer is JSON with the result under `data`; a list also has `cursor`, the next page's cursor or null. An error is an RFC 9457 problem document, `application/problem+json`, with `type`, `title`, `status`, `code` and `detail`, and `pointer` when one field is at fault.

Requests sign in as WordPress core accepts: the logged-in cookie with an `X-WP-Nonce` header, an application password, or a TypedPress Identity access token. Each operation says who may call it. A field the caller may not read is left out of rows, and can't be filtered or sorted on.

`typedpress build` writes this document from the app's schema, with the typed client in `tp/_generated/client/` and the app's WordPress Abilities; a component here has the name of the client's type for the same value.

get.description:
The pages rows the caller may read, one page at a time. `limit` is 50 unless given, and at most 100; `cursor` is null on the last page.

Access: A rule in the app's code decides who may do this, and for which rows.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: A filter, as JSON: a value or operators per field, with `AND`, `OR` and `NOT`. A filter on a field the caller may not read is refused.

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: Fields to sort by, comma-separated; `-` before a field sorts it descending (`-createdAt,title`). Fields: `id`, `title`, `slug`, `body`, `cover`, `featured`, `seo`, `sections`, `status`, `publishedAt`, `uid`, `locale`, `translations`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Words to find, each at the start of a word, in the title, the content and every text field the caller may read. Only rows the caller may read are found, in the list's own order.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only rows with this status; shorthand for a filter on `status`.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: What to load with each row, comma-separated or as a JSON object: `activity`, `cover`. A relation holds only rows the caller may read.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: The rows of one locale, with each translation group's fallback where it has none; `*` for every row. Without it, the default locale.

post.description:
Creates one pages row and returns it.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

get.description:
One pages row.

Access: A rule in the app's code decides who may do this, and for which rows.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: What to load with each row, comma-separated or as a JSON object: `activity`, `cover`. A relation holds only rows the caller may read.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: The rows of one locale, with each translation group's fallback where it has none; `*` for every row. Without it, the default locale.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `md` answers with the row as Markdown (`text/markdown`) instead of JSON.

patch.description:
Changes the fields sent on one pages row and returns the row.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

delete.description:
Deletes one pages row for good and returns the row as it was.

Access: Users with the `admin` role or a higher one may do this.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: _rev
parameters.description: The `_rev` of your read: the delete is refused with `409 stale_revision` if the row changed since.

parameters.name: takeover
parameters.description: `1` takes over another user's edit lock.

get.description:
Each saved version of the row, newest first, with its time and who saved it, one page at a time. `limit` is 50 unless given, and at most 100; `cursor` is null on the last page.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

get.description:
The row as this revision saved it.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision's id.

post.description:
Makes the revision the current row, as an update of the row.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; a row outside it is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision's id.

get.description:
The row as it would be once promoted, the fields that are staged, and who staged last. With `preview=<token>` it answers without signing in, through an anonymous visitor's field masks.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: A preview token from the preview route.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

_rev.description: The staged version's token, for the next stage, promote or discard.

patch.description:
Saves the fields sent into the row's staged version. The live row stays as it is until the staged version is promoted. Checked as an update would be; no hook runs.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

_rev.description: The staged version's token, for the next stage, promote or discard.

delete.summary: Discard the staged version of pages
delete.description:
Ends the staged version. The live row is untouched; the discarded version stays in the row's revisions.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

parameters.name: _rev
parameters.description: The staged version's `_rev`: the discard is refused with `409 stale_revision` if it changed since.

parameters.name: takeover
parameters.description: `1` takes over another user's edit lock.

get.description:
The staged fields whose value differs from the live row, with both values, as the caller may read each side.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

_rev.description: The staged version's token, for the next stage, promote or discard.

post.summary: Promote the staged version of pages
post.description:
Makes the staged version live, as an update of the row by the caller: its rules, hooks, unique checks and webhooks run. With `at` (a future time) the promote is scheduled instead, and `at: null` cancels a scheduled one; both answer with the staged version.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

requestBody.description: Empty, or `at`; `_rev` and `takeover` as on a stage.

200.description: The row after the promote, or the staged version when `at` was sent.

id.description: The revision that holds the staged version.

_rev.description: The staged version's token, for the next stage, promote or discard.

post.description:
A signed link to the staged version that works without signing in until it expires (an hour by default, a day at most) or the staged version is promoted or discarded.

Access: Users with the `editor` role or a higher one may do this.

Needs the kind's update rule on the row; anyone else gets the 404 of a missing row, whether or not something is staged.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The row's id, or `slug:<slug>` for the row with that slug.

api.description: Reads the staged version without signing in.

url.description: The row's own page showing the staged version, when the theme renders it.
